text_blocks.snippet: Newcastle disease virus (NDV) is a highly contagious and often fatal virus that affects a wide range of bird species, including domestic poultry and some wild birds. It is caused by virulent strains of the virus, and different strains can cause varying degrees of severity. While the virus primarily affects birds, humans can experience mild conjunctivitis and influenza-like symptoms from exposure.
snippet_highlighted_words: a highly contagious and often fatal virus that affects a wide range of bird species, including domestic poultry and some wild birds

list.title: Highly Contagious:
list.snippet: NDV spreads easily among susceptible birds through respiratory secretions, feces, and contaminated objects.

list.title: Wide Range of Hosts:
list.snippet: While chickens are highly susceptible, the virus can affect over 250 bird species, including waterfowl, which are less susceptible.

list.title: Varying Severity:
list.snippet: Different strains of NDV exhibit varying levels of virulence, with some causing severe illness and high mortality rates, while others are less pathogenic.
